info.title: Neosian storage HTTP contract
info.description: Storage wire 6, independent of package version. Bodies are JSON objects regardless of Content-Type; legacy operations ignore unknown request keys and treat optional null as absence. Optional memory-search version 1 uses strict fields and types, with null allowed only for cursor. Optional turn-records version 1 routes are strict too, with null allowed only where a field's schema admits it, and conversation/write_records takes a body of at most 4194304 bytes. JSON Schema describes supported typed input, not legacy coercions. Scope/conversation allowances are literal prefixes; constrained tokens cannot call store/* or /mcp and must explicitly bound conversation searches/trail reads. MCP at /mcp is a separate negotiated protocol, not described by this document. Large answers are produced completely before the status line and sent with Content-Length, so every refusal is an ordinary status and envelope.

authorization.description: Optional opt-in grant enforcement capability, versioned separately from wire 6. Required by portable HTTP profiles.

memory_search.description: Optional current-memory lexical search contract version 1. Its absence means memory/search is unsupported.

memory_ranking.description: Optional memory ranking version 1 on memory/search: relevance and newest orders and updated_since/updated_before bounds. Requires memory_search version 1. No new access authority.

memory_passages.description: Optional memory passages version 1 on memory/search: up to three matched windows per hit from long content or metadata values, each with its nearest heading. Requires memory_search version 1. No new access authority.

history_ranking.description: Optional history ranking version 1 on conversation/search_turns: relevance and newest orders and since/before turn-time bounds. No new access authority.

knowledge_policy.description: Optional governance format-1 filtering on memory/search. Requires memory_search version 1. No new access authority.

change_feed.description: Optional durable scope changes and operator retention, format 1.

size_paging.description: Optional size paging version 1 on conversation/search_turns and conversation/read_turns: page_bytes bounds a page to the whole turns that fit (always at least one) and an opaque continuation carries the rest. The server caps page_bytes at its own ceiling. No new access authority.

post.description: Read turns after a number, oldest first. An explicit limit <= 500 is a total bound and returns next_after null; omitted/larger limits can page. Size paging version 1 adds page_bytes and continuation: a size-paged page holds at most 500 turns, an explicit limit bounds the total across pages, and next_after is null because continuation alone continues.

page_bytes.description: Size paging version 1. The page's byte ceiling: the page holds whole turns in answer order while their compact JSON encodings together stay within it, counting each turn's UTF-8 bytes, and always at least one turn. A server serves a larger value as its own ceiling. A request carrying it is size-paged and its answer adds continuation.

continuation.description: Size paging version 1. The continuation of the previous page, sent back with the same request; requires page_bytes. It binds the request's selection (a different selection is value_error) and confers no permission.
Size paging version 1, present only in an answer to a request carrying page_bytes: an opaque token to send back for the next page, or null when no turn remains.

post.description: Version 1: every whitespace-split term must occur as a case-insensitive substring; newest first. Blank queries are refused. Omitted conversations selects all; [] selects none. No paging. History ranking version 1 adds order, since and before. Size paging version 1 adds page_bytes and continuation: limit then bounds the total across pages; newest and version 1 continue by keyset, and relevance counts again over the unpaged selection and refuses with value_error when the candidate turns changed. Each page repeats the search's scan.

order.description: History ranking version 1. Absent or null is version 1 newest without an echo. newest is the version 1 answer within the bounds. relevance takes candidate turns holding at least one term under the backend's version 1 matching and scores them with the memory-ranking BM25 arithmetic over the candidate set, counting occurrences in the searchable text after Unicode lowercase; ties follow the newest total order.

since.description: History ranking version 1. Inclusive lower bound on turn created_at: a UTC RFC 3339 instant ending in Z.

before.description: History ranking version 1. Exclusive upper bound on turn created_at, UTC ending in Z; since must precede it. Turns are immutable, so this is an exact as-of cutoff.

page_bytes.description: Size paging version 1. The page's byte ceiling: the page holds whole turns in answer order while their compact JSON encodings together stay within it, counting each turn's UTF-8 bytes, and always at least one turn. A server serves a larger value as its own ceiling. A request carrying it is size-paged and its answer adds continuation.

continuation.description: Size paging version 1. The continuation of the previous page, sent back with the same request; requires page_bytes. It binds the request's selection (a different selection is value_error) and confers no permission.

order.description: History ranking version 1: echoes an explicit request order; absent when the request names no order.

scores.description: Relevance order only: round-half-even(BM25 x 10^6) per turn, parallel to turns and non-increasing.

continuation.description: Size paging version 1, present only in an answer to a request carrying page_bytes: an opaque token to send back for the next page, or null when no turn remains.

omitted.description: Only where turns are stored as records: how many matching turns too long to answer whole (past the server's NEOSIAN_MAX_TURN_BYTES) keep their place among the winners without being answered. The last key, absent when none; on a size page, those the page passed.

post.summary: Search current memory in one authorized scope (optional version 1; memory ranking version 1 adds orders and date bounds)

query.description: 1..16 whitespace terms, matched as per-scalar Unicode 17.0.0 lowercase substrings across selected values. Version 1, path and newest orders need every term; memory ranking relevance needs at least one. No stemming, normalization or regex.

prefix.description: Case-sensitive literal document-path prefix, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes.

cursor.description: Opaque keyset continuation bound to scope, query, prefix, fields and metadata keys. Not a permission token or snapshot. Review policy is also bound; expiry and revocation are rechecked per page.

knowledge_policy.description: Optional knowledge_policy capability version 1; filter current review state at server UTC before matching and pagination. All preserves unfiltered behavior.

order.description: Memory ranking version 1. Absent or null is version 1 path order without an echo. relevance scores documents holding at least one term with pinned BM25; newest orders all-terms matches by updated_at descending. Both return at most limit hits with a null cursor; cursors continue path order only.

updated_since.description: Memory ranking version 1. Inclusive lower bound on the current version's updated_at: a UTC RFC 3339 instant ending in Z. Bound into path cursors.

updated_before.description: Memory ranking version 1. Exclusive upper bound on updated_at, UTC ending in Z; updated_since must precede it. Bound into path cursors.

passages.description: Memory passages version 1. 1..3 gives every hit a passages array, possibly empty; absent, null or 0 keeps version 1 hits. Passages never change matching, order, scores or cursors.

schema.description: Requires memory_search version 1. Unknown fields and mistyped/default-null fields refuse. metadata requires 1..8 metadata_keys; keys require the metadata field. Scope authorization precedes scanning and pagination.

excerpt.description: Up to 240 original Unicode scalars, starting up to 40 scalars before the first match. Offset is zero-based within the path, body or matched metadata string value. Content is preferred, then selected metadata keys, then path.

score.description: Relevance order only: round-half-even(BM25 x 10^6), BM25 over version 1 substring occurrence counts with k1 1.2 and b 0.75, statistics from the eligible selection of this scope.

passages.description: Memory passages version 1, present only when requested. Windows of selected content or metadata values longer than 240 scalars: each starts 40 scalars before an occurrence and spans at most 240; chosen greedily by distinct terms inside, then occurrences inside, then value order and offset, never overlapping within a value; listed in value order, then offset.

heading.description: Content only: the nearest ATX heading starting at or before the window, outside fenced code and a leading frontmatter or comment block; null otherwise.

order.description: Memory ranking version 1: echoes an explicit request order; absent for version 1 requests.

schema.description: Version 1: ascending document-path order; a nonfinal page has exactly limit hits; no total count. Memory ranking version 1: relevance sorts by score descending, then path; newest by updated_at descending, then path; both return at most limit hits with a null next_cursor. Only current, non-redacted memory documents are searched. sessions/, messages/, message-links/ and handoff are excluded. Each page reads current state; writes before the last key require a new query.

post.summary: Write one part of a turn as records into a draft, or probe, seal or discard it (optional turn records version 1)

draft.description: Chosen by the client, unique within the conversation.

records.description: Consecutive seq; empty for a probe or a discard.

turn_bytes.description: The bytes the sealed turn's header will carry; stated at the opening or repeated unchanged.

200.description: Success; keys in this order; at most 2048 + 6 * u(actor) bytes for the draft's stamped actor

stored_bytes.description: Size-rule bytes this request added; 0 for a pure repeat.

400.description: Invalid parameters, a draft conflict (agent_conversation_conflict with a reason), or agent_configuration_error on a store without records

401.description: Missing or invalid bearer; plain text, not the JSON envelope

413.description: Body exceeds 4194304 bytes, or the turn exceeds the store's NEOSIAN_MAX_RECORD_TURN_BYTES (value_error); a gateway or custom backend may answer storage_exceeded

500.description: Internal/driver error, plain text with no storage envelope

post.summary: Read a conversation's turns as records under a view, paged by bytes (optional turn records version 1)

turn.description: This turn only; excludes after and through.

after.description: Turns after this number; excluded by turn, also when 0.

through.description: Turns up to this number, inclusive.

seq.description: Start at this record; requires turn.

piece.description: Only the piece holding record seq, all its chunks, whatever heads says; requires turn and seq, also when false.

kinds.description: The kinds answered, as a set: order and repeats do not matter; all eight when absent, headers only when empty.

heads.description: Kind to bytes: a piece of that kind whose text encodes to more than twice the bytes is answered as one record holding its head and tail.

page_bytes.description: The page's byte ceiling, served at most the server's NEOSIAN_MAX_PAGE_BYTES: a page holds headers and records while their compact encodings, one separator each, stay within it, and always at least one group: a record with its turn's header, or the header alone of a turn with no record selected.

continuation.description: The previous page's continuation, sent back with the same selection; page_bytes may differ. 1 to 4096 UTF-8 bytes: the server counts bytes, so maxLength, which counts characters, is necessary and not sufficient (a continuation the server issued is ASCII). Another selection, or a place outside this request's selection, is value_error. It names a place and confers no permission.

200.description: Success; keys in this order: turns, records, continuation; at most max(min(page_bytes, NEOSIAN_MAX_PAGE_BYTES), 81920 + h) + 4160 bytes, h being the first header of the page, at most 192 + 6 * u(actor)

turns.description: The header of every turn the page reaches, in turn order, with records on it or passed with none selected.

records.description: In (turn, seq) order, filtered by kinds.

continuation.description: Null on the last page; otherwise ASCII, 1 to 4096 bytes.

400.description: Invalid parameters, a continuation of another selection (value_error), a stored turn that cannot be read as records (agent_conversation_format_unsupported), or agent_configuration_error on a store without records
